clue.text: Less certain, midwife going to and fro expressed hesitation

indicators.note: travelling there and back says the middle of 'wife' is read forwards and then backwards, a run that reads the same both ways

parts.note: read as 'mid wife', the middle letters of the word wife, IF, which then goes there and back
er is the sound a speaker makes when hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone describes a midwife pacing up and down, hesitant and unsure.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'midwife' as 'mid wife': the middle of WIFE is IF. 'Going to and fro' sends it forward and back, IF then FI, before ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful, so the comparative means more doubtful.

clue.text: It serves to illustrate batting position

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
a stance is the way one stands, a posture or position

explanation.surface: A cricket coach shows how a batsman should stand at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: An example cited to show a point is a case in point, which illustrates it.

clue.text: Having a month to figure out a remedy

parts.note: Feb is the short form of February

indicators.note: figure out here means the letters of figure are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spends a month working out a cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine that reduces fever is a remedy for that condition.

clue.text: Auditors discovering Antony's loan request?

explanation.surface: Accountants uncover what Antony asked to borrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Antony's speech in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar begins 'Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears'.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditors are listeners, and the organs of hearing are what Antony asked the crowd to lend him.

clue.text: Complaint about rough bar of soap?

indicators.note: about says the word for the complaint goes round the other letters

parts.note: colic is a stomach complaint, an illness

indicators.note: rough suggests the letters of bar are roughed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A grumble about a coarse cake of soap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' turns BAR into ARB, which 'about' puts inside COLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbolic soap is a disinfectant soap made with phenol, an old household staple.

clue.text: Mortifying the flesh, like team dropping fullback

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of

indicators.note: dropping means the letter is left out of the team's name

parts.note: Celtic is a Glasgow football team
read as 'full back', the back or last letter of the word full

explanation.surface: Self-denial is compared to a football side that leaves out its defender.
explanation.walkthrough: A fullback is a defender in football, but here the 'back' of FULL is L, which 'dropping' takes out of CELTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic denies the body comforts and pleasures as self-discipline, the sense of mortifying the flesh.

clue.text: Astonished to see bird in hat

indicators.note: in says the bird sits inside the hat

parts.note: a bowler is a hard round felt hat
a dove is a bird of the pigeon family

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed at a bird sitting in a hat, like a magician's trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowled over is an idiom for overwhelmed with surprise.

clue.text: Isabel or Natalie: a little girl's name

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Isabel or Natalie are offered as examples of a little girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorna is a female first name, made popular by the novel Lorna Doone.

clue.text: Baby lettuce place

parts.note: cos is a variety of long-leaved lettuce
to set is to place or put down

explanation.surface: A little lettuce is planted in its spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baby' reads as an adjective describing the lettuce, but it is a verb, to pamper.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper someone is to treat them indulgently, as one would an infant.

clue.text: Empty tent — a shelter outside for PM

indicators.note: outside says these pieces go round the letters from the empty tent

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind

indicators.note: an empty tent has nothing inside, leaving just its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A campaigning politician sleeps in an empty tent with a shelter round it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' leaves TT from TENT, and 'outside' puts A and LEE around it. Clement Attlee was the UK Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee was British Prime Minister after the Second World War.

clue.text: New city bar is far from 5

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A newly opened city bar is anything but austere.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CITY BAR IS are rearranged. 5 is ASCETIC, self-denying, and a sybarite is its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybaritic means devoted to luxury and pleasure, the opposite of self-denying austerity.

clue.text: Opera factory

explanation.surface: An opera house doubles as a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is the Latin plural of opus, an artist's compositions, and a plant or mill is also called this.

clue.text: A song about a song

indicators.note: about says the word for the song is turned round

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: One song is about another song.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic solo for one voice is a song.

clue.text: A genius, initially of normal intelligence, outside in

indicators.note: outside says the phrase for normal intelligence goes round the A and the initial

parts.note: all there is an idiom for mentally sound, with one's wits

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word genius is taken

explanation.surface: A clever person, at first average, is placed outside or in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives G from 'genius'; A and G go inside ALL THERE, which 'outside' places around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashionable things are said to be in, and the phrase means highly fashionable.

clue.text: A male's been taken off by mariners

indicators.note: taken off suggests the letters are disturbed and moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A man has been removed from a ship by its sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Able seamen are rated sailors, so they are mariners.

clue.text: Confectioner's first to discover truth about sweet

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the confectioner is used

parts.note: to rumble someone is British slang for finding out what they are up to

explanation.surface: A sweet-maker is the first to learn the truth about a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: To rumble someone is British slang for seeing through them. A crumble is a baked fruit pudding with a crumbly topping.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit crumble is a British pudding, and a sweet is the dessert course.

clue.text: Flocks of birds — about 500

indicators.note: about says the birds go round the numeral

parts.note: crows are black birds
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: About five hundred birds make up a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: To flock is to gather in large numbers, so masses of people are throngs.

clue.text: Resident composer for old Medici?

indicators.note: a composer for these letters arranges them, so the words old and Medici are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A house composer is retained by the old Medici family of Florence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Medici were the ruling family of Renaissance Florence, famous as patrons of the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Domiciled means having a fixed home somewhere, as a resident does.

clue.text: A parrot aboard a destroyer

parts.note: Polly is the stock pet name for a parrot
on means aboard, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A parrot rides on a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Revelation, Apollyon is the angel of the abyss, whose name means the destroyer.

clue.text: Old traveller in tavern because every second counts

indicators.note: every second says only alternate letters of the words are kept, starting from the second

explanation.surface: An ancient wanderer drinks in a tavern because every moment matters.
explanation.walkthrough: Aeneas is the Trojan hero of Virgil's Aeneid, who wandered for years before reaching Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeneas fled Troy and journeyed across the Mediterranean, an ancient voyager of legend.

clue.text: Excellent woman, right?

parts.note: Stella is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a woman is first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar means starry, and so outstanding or first-rate.

clue.text: Conceive — and have pram due for delivery?

indicators.note: for delivery suggests the letters are sent out in a new order

explanation.surface: Expecting parents get a pram ready as the baby is due.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a baby due to be delivered; the letters of PRAM DUE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream up an idea is to invent it, to think it up.

clue.text: Money dumb physician left to animals

indicators.note: left means the physician has departed from the word dumb

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
cats are animals

explanation.surface: A mute doctor leaves his money to his pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like the bequest in the surface, but it takes MB out of DUMB, leaving DU.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducats were gold coins used across Europe, so they stand for cash.

clue.text: Fasteners for propellers

explanation.surface: Fixings are offered as ship propellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Threaded fixings are this, and a ship's propeller is also called this.

clue.text: Get-together to discuss a pear

explanation.surface: A meeting convenes to debate a single pear.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal meeting for debate goes by this name, and it is also a popular English variety of pear.

clue.text: Mean street in any settlement?

indicators.note: in says the street goes inside the rearranged letters
settlement suggests the letters of any are settled into a new order

explanation.surface: A mean street can be found in any town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement?' turns ANY into NAY, and 'in' puts ST inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty and mean both describe someone unkind or spiteful.

clue.text: A company letterhead reveals system for winning contracts

parts.note: the head of the word letter is its first letter, L

explanation.surface: A firm's headed notepaper reveals a method of landing business deals.
explanation.walkthrough: Contracts here are bridge contracts: Acol is the bidding system most used in British bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Acol is a bidding system in bridge, used to reach and make contracts.

clue.text: Exuberance in the centre of Cambridge on the first of October

indicators.note: the centre of says the three middle letters of Cambridge are taken
the first of means only the opening letter of October is used

explanation.surface: High spirits fill Cambridge at the start of the October term.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour or liveliness, as in playing music with spirit.

clue.text: Parking in some odd spot in Surrey

indicators.note: in says the parking letter goes inside the rearranged letters
odd suggests the letters of some are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: Someone parks in a strange place somewhere in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' turns SOME into ESOM, and 'in' puts P inside it. Surrey is a county south of London; Epsom is a town there famous for its racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is a Surrey town, home of the Derby racecourse.

clue.text: Succeeding with partner on the side

parts.note: later means coming after, succeeding in time
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: Someone makes progress with a partner they have on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Laterally means sideways, toward or from one flank.

clue.text: Farewell, for example, before Aaron goes off

parts.note: say means for example

indicators.note: goes off suggests the letters of Aaron explode into a new order

explanation.surface: People say goodbye before Aaron departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sayonara is the Japanese word for goodbye.

clue.text: Love God without appearing unnatural

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the god goes round the zero

parts.note: Woden is the Anglo-Saxon chief god
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: Love of God without any show of feeling seems unnatural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking: WODEN is put around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden performance is stiff and stilted rather than natural.
